reviews.text: Endearing but tonally spotty, The Little Mermaid (2023) lacks the whimsy of the original but finds a star-making performance in Halle Bailey.
reviews.author: Isabella Liistro

reviews.text: Halle Bailey is doing her damndest, in spite of underwater CGI effects that frankly make her look like a waxwork.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: The result is another mixed bag that may contain some rare pearls within its shell but can only dream of being part of its animated counterpart’s world.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: The film feels at once too stunted for an actual musical and too expansive to be just another movie.
reviews.author: Savina Petkova

reviews.text: The music does seem to soar for the most part, and the movie is all elevated by Halle Bailey, she's fantastic.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: [U]nfortunately, you do gotta (slightly) hand it to them — in the disenchanting, decomposing pile of animated adaptations, The Little Mermaid at least lies somewhere in the upper half.
reviews.author: Jackson Weaver

reviews.text: It can go without saying but Halle Bailey as Ariel is the most perfect casting for a live-action remake Disney has ever done. The way she was able to capture Ariel’s child-like inquisitiveness, stubbornness & yearning is something that should be studied.
reviews.author: Shanelle Genai

reviews.text: The delightful sits alongside the baffling in Marshall’s adaptation, which is so often the way it goes with these Disney live action remakes.
reviews.author: Caroline Siede

reviews.text: Consider the lousy animation and awkward performances and highly questionable narrative and ask what, to the tune of “Under the Sea,” the hell is this?
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: To begin, Halle Bailey. Remember her name and don’t forget it. From the trailers, to the red carpet, under the sea and above it, she is charismatic, humble, and a songstress.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Peterson

reviews.text: By making a series of small changes and using his experience in adapting musicals ("Chicago"/"Into the Woods"), [director Rob] Marshall crafts a story we know and gives it an entirely different vibe, for better or worse.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Halle Bailey is by far the best part of Rob Marshall’s 2023 live action movie. She is a luminous talent with an angelic voice. She is without a doubt Ariel with her wide-eyed wonder and teen rebellion.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: Another popcorn summer film, this time inviting a dive into the cool CGI waters of Atlantica peppered with shark attacks, shipwrecks and a giant octopus sea witch. Empty calories definitely, but fun all the same
reviews.author: Mini Anthikad-Chhibber

reviews.text: All the film’s flaws and miscalculations can be forgiven by its most impressive saving grace: Bailey’s performance is as remarkable as it is enchanting.
reviews.author: Lee Zumpe

reviews.text: ...looks like a cheapie commercial for Royal Caribbean Cruises.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: [Bailey] is absolutely magnetic on the screen and it’s hard to imagine many others being as perfect for the role as she turns out to be.
reviews.author: Max Covill

reviews.text: The casting, new songs and overall look aren’t strong enough to promote or weak enough to disparage.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: It’s a weird message to be sending children these days: pretend to be something you’re not, keep your trap shut and hope nobody notices the scales.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Nothing in recent memory feels so much like amalgamated groupthink capital-C Content like this Little Mermaid.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid enriches virtually every narrative aspect compared to the original, deepening Ariel and Eric's arcs while exploring the same core themes without losing any of its predecessor's essence.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid (2023) is the most successful of the live-action Disney remakes. Even with its shortcomings, the heart of the animated film exists within this new version which cannot be said for many other live action remakes.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Mostly thanks to the music and dramatic performances from Bailey and McCarthy, "The Little Mermaid" goes along swimmingly. And that puts it several strokes ahead of other live-action Disney remakes.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: Although it does not possess the same campy nature as its animated predecessor, The Little Mermaid maintains the emotion of the beloved story through a star-creating performance and emphasis on relationships.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: I never saw the original [Disney's Little Mermaid], so I have no frame of reference and can't say if it's better or not. For me, this was a so-so movie...The songs are fun, but didn't have the magic or the heart that you'd expect from Disney.
reviews.author: Michael Cook

reviews.text: Halle Bailey was born to be a Disney Princess INCREDIBLE! The visuals were pretty solid and the songs were great. It’s not without It’s flaws and a bit too long but overall, I’m very excited for everyone to see Halle bring this classic princess to life.
reviews.author: Elliott Collins

reviews.text: When 'Under the Sea' echoes against a literal sea of colour, movement, creatures and energy, it's a dazzling Golden Age Hollywood-esque spectacular. There's no escaping the movie's bloat when it's not merrily floating, however.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: It is hard to see too many fans of the original The Little Mermaid being disappointed in this adaption. The classic songs are there, and delivered in unique re-workings, with some extras also thrown in.
reviews.author: David Griffiths

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid is the perfect movie for newcomers to the story… for adults who love the original they may not feel the magic the same way. One thing everyone should agree on though is Halle Bailey's incredible performance.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: "Whether Disney will use its profits to pay its writers fairly and invest in original Black stories is yet to be seen. But a win is a win, and we deserve it."
reviews.author: Brooke Obie

reviews.text: Among the core characters, Halle Bailey as Ariel and Melissa McCarthy as Ursula truly stand out. Bailey flawlessly embodies the titular character...
reviews.author: Tyler Strandberg

reviews.text: I wish I could write that ‘The Little Mermaid” unreels swimmingly, but I can’t. It's billed as live-action; however, there’s a lot of CGI and the entire enterprise is weighed down by a digitized watery palette that doesn’t look its best.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text:
The new live-action version of “The Little Mermaid” is so stuffed with extraneous characters, lavish orchestrations and special effects, you wonder if there’s room to move.

Too many fish in the sea, you might say.
reviews.author: Bruce R. Miller

reviews.text: Halley Bailey's star power is the only thing worth your time.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: Parts of this movie are truly enchanting, especially the underwater scenes. The opening moments on Prince Eric’s ship are thrillingly filmed and the “Under the Sea” number is a glorious Busby Berkeley underwater fantasia.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: What, exactly, is the point of trying to redo masterpieces from the golden age of Disney animation with modern CGI tech?
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid conserves some of the stronger points from the original movie.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: [Bailey's] voice is incredible and her acting as the adventurous, opinionated and naive Ariel is superb. She is a joy to watch... However, the script, dialogue and editing of the film is another story.
reviews.author: Maan Jalal

reviews.text: Halle Bailey has incredible stage presence and most of the retread material is fine. The real sin here is Disney's continued employment of Rob Marshall.
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: On one hand, it’s just more of the same for Disney: be true to yourself; follow your heart; don’t let anyone stand in your way ... But especially against the backdrop of our current cultural moment, the 2023 Mermaid takes it one step further.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: It’s trying so hard to not upset fans of the original that it often feels like imitation with a couple of adjustments. And that’s about as flat as Flounder’s new-found photorealism.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: The teenage protagonists and lengthy run time might exclude smaller children from the equation, but a fun family film is still on the ticket.
reviews.author: Gemma Creagh

reviews.text: Since the film’s announcement, this mermaid has been swimming against the current of controversy and backlash, but this movie does a good enough job that it grants a viewing.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: Halle Bailey is spectacular in this modern adaptation of Disney's beloved story. A live-action film that preserves the magic of the animated classic while allowing itself to find its own identity. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: The great news about “The Little Mermaid” is that a star has been born in Halle Bailey’s performance, and the lovely singing voice carries the film along with the supporting cast.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: It is all a little waterlogged but Bailey andMcCarthy make it spring back to life.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: I enjoyed this remake of “The Little Mermaid,” and I think the live action realism enhances the romance of the story.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: All the narrative tweaks make it more convoluted than it needs to be... It just made me want to rewatch the original.
reviews.author: Manuel Betancourt

reviews.text: It's pretty hard to come close to perfection... This is definitely not better than the original, but it doesn't tarnish it, either.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: As far as Disney live-action remakes go, this certainly fares better than some of the other entries in recent years.
reviews.author: Marriska Fernandes

reviews.text: A transparently corporate exercise in studio-mandated money-spinning, this bloated remake fails to better its beloved source material in any way...
reviews.author: Joel Harley

reviews.text: A betwixt-and-between movie — never recapturing the magic of the 1989 original when it follows too closely, and never quite succeeding in creating anything fresh where it tries to diverge from its predecessor.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: One of Disney's best live-action remakes so far.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: Broadly unnecessary and only fitfully justified by production values or lead performances ....
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: When it works, it's enjoyable and entertaining…when it doesn’t work, it can be a slog - one that does not justify its overly long runtime. Halle Bailey is a star in the lead role, but the rest of the movie does not live up to her promise.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: An exemplar of the Walt Disney Company's ongoing attempt to take what is beautifully expressive and aesthetically rich about its unmatched canon of animated features stretching back to 1937, and turn it into grey paste
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid (2023) is one of the best Disney live action remakes.
reviews.author: Jake Peffer

reviews.text: The update on the beloved classic Disney animation has a longer run time, harbours some murkier depths with an enhanced sea witch, but it has less of the zing and energy of the original
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: The mermaids look cool, Halle Bailey is great, and the target tween audience might find enough here to satisfy. Adults, though, will be dead bored.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Scuttling, sentimental fantasy, specifically geared to 'woke' 2023, when audiences may want to see a more dutiful, diversity-aware approach to race and gender.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Miranda and Menken’s musical partnership does breathe fresh life into the story with new songs that honor Howard Ashman’s work to give Ariel a voice...
reviews.author: Sabina Graves

reviews.text: Overall, it’s a visually gorgeous film, buoyed by a strong ingenue in Bailey with enough laughs for the kids and the nostalgic adults—just don’t expect anything new.
reviews.author: Noëlle D. Lilley

reviews.text: This remake fails to fix one key criticism of the original Little Mermaid: the sexist message that women must transform themselves to fit into their man's world...
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: Bailey is terrific, a star-to-be, in this update of a 186-year-old fairytale.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: While The Little Mermaid certainly isn’t breaking new ground in the musical department, it manages to be a fun times at the movies and audiences will surely get their fill
reviews.author: Terence Johnson

reviews.text: This version lacks the same spark, despite a lot of high energy throughout the song. It just falls flat and serves as a reminder how much inferior this version is to the original.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Is The Little Mermaid good? I have no idea how to answer that question.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Halle Bailey as Ariel is a superb choice, with an expressive voice and a commitment to the role, and Melissa McCarthy as Ursula puts her ankles into it, showing proper respect to both Pat Carroll and the late Divine.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: Is this movie anywhere near as good as the 1989 animated film? Absolutely not. However, this is also not the disaster that some may expect. For what it did on its own, it’s not bad.
reviews.author: Mat Brunet

reviews.text: In theory, this trend of adapting these classics for a new audience with new technology and a contemporary eye is a worthy endeavor. As of yet, though (with the exception of Cinderella), no one tasked with this mission has completed it successfully.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: "The Little Mermaid" creates a splash.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Despite a few notable warts, The Little Mermaid manages to justify its own existence thanks to Bailey’s strong work as Ariel, some technical wizardry and Marshall’s musical acumen.
reviews.author: Joshua Axelrod

reviews.text: Rob Marshall's no-risk reboot avoids pushing along conversations of identity, belonging or choice.
reviews.author: Udita Jhunjhunwala

reviews.text: Romantic and social drama ignite this ode to love, tolerance and acceptance.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: That epic battle is the film's lowest low point (trust, there are others), in which Marshall forgot he was making a Disney movie and decided to dabble in some Marvel mayhem.
reviews.author: Gregg Shapiro

reviews.text: The crab does indeed look more like a crab and the fish does indeed look like a fish, but the infinitely more joyous expressiveness of the hand-drawn animation has now been replaced by cold, dead eyes.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: Like many before it, Marshall’s film takes a snappy animated caper and stretches it beyond breaking point. But two of our leads do decent, commendable work. I suppose that’s something, right?​
reviews.author: Chris Wasser

reviews.text: Dazzling and wondrous, The Little Mermaid makes a solid transition to become a part of Disney’s live-action world of remakes.
reviews.author: Mark McPherson

reviews.text: Bailey is hampered by a weak subplot about her rebellion against King Triton, and yet she still manages to carry this vehicle easily. This remake would sink without her star quality.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid is devoid of all wonder as if it had been dictated by the higher-ups to do so out of fear that they might, somehow, make a better movie than the original.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: The memorable songs are here, performances are charming and there are flashy visual effects, but director Rob Marshall loses clarity and resonance in the under-lit settings, swooping-shaking camerawork and shredder-style editing.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Melissa McCarthy is incredible... she's a lot of fun.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: This is an absolutely delightful picture and is quite possibly my favorite of all the princess live-action remakes. Much of that is due to the powerful performance -- and singing chops -- of lead Halle Bailey as Ariel.
reviews.author: Erik Kain

reviews.text:
The Little Mermaid is solid. It’s carried by Halle Bailey incredible vocal performance, which represented the best of the film.

Still, like all Disney Remakes, you see diminished returns of the superior animated original.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: ...it doesn't present a good argument for its existence, creatively.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Halle Bailey’s turn as The Little Mermaid’s Ariel is inspired, but the movie’s lackluster sense of visual magic does her very few favors.
reviews.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore

reviews.text: Feels like something is missing. That’s the magic that made the ink and paint Little Mermaid an enduring classic.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: ... Despite its present effectiveness, this live-action pass doesn't offer new meanings or contributions that will make the film stand the test of time. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: The new Little Mermaid is somehow 135 minutes long, a whopping 52 more than the lean animated version, but it adds almost nothing of note to the mix, largely spending that extra time on stretched-out action sequences and slightly more plot context.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid is a dank, lethargic cash grab that feels like a glimpse of that bleakest possible future. While David Magee gets credit for the script here, it’s the kind of film that could easily be written by a ChatGPT type program.
reviews.author: Melanie Fischer

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid is thoroughly enjoyable, owing much of this to Bailey’s irrepressible charm and crystal clear vocals, and her chemistry with all of her castmates.
reviews.author: Carolyn Hinds

reviews.text: Bailey is so luminous that it's easy to overlook just how bland everything else around her is.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Thanks to Halle Bailey, Jonah Hauer-King, and some key changes in the script, it’s undoubtedly one of Disney’s most interesting, ambitious remakes yet.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: Halle Bailey floats to the surface in her heartfelt vocals, vibrant performance and natural charm. While this reimagining had a lot of interesting trinkets, it dulled in comparison to her sparkle and shine.
reviews.author: KT Mahe

reviews.text: Halle Bailey's compelling portrayal of Ariel emerges as a highlight. Her exquisite vocals and perfect embodiment of the character imbue a sense of grace, despite the live-action adaptation's struggle to capture the original's vibrance.
reviews.author: Oti

reviews.text: It wades into the choppy waters of the current discourse and emerges a lackluster Disney remake with the courage of its convictions.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: One of the better Disney live-action remakes, but still suffers from redundancy.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: These Disney remakes are like cover versions of songs, so don’t expect it to reinvent the wheel. However, there are some great casting decisions in there.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: An entertaining enough film that justifies its longer runtime with a more detailed focus on its central romance. I don't think it's the definitive version, but it's still a pretty faithful and satisfying and fun adaptation. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Everything underwater looks like a bad deepfake, each new song is worse than the last, the Under the Sea number is like a Baz Luhrmann vomitorium and an unbearable additional 50 minutes make this an all-around atrocity.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: Disney’s new live-action take on The Little Mermaid goes along swimmingly in its sweet romance, but it doesn’t diverge enough from its animated roots to truly make a splash. ... adorable enough in parts, but its story largely stays on the surface.
reviews.author: Valerie Kalfrin

reviews.text: 'The Little Mermaid' follows the counters of its animated predecessor rather faithfully. It includes a couple of new songs and a bit-too-long, but lively, dance sequence, but they do not detract from the overall production.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Bailey is terrific but the film around her grows dull and muddy.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid will no doubt be a hit for Disney, and they have faith in it, or else it would have been expelled to the Neverland that is Disney+, but it is far from the exceptional experience they presented us back in 1989.
reviews.author: Erin Maxwell

reviews.text: This is one for the whole family - any family to enjoy and to sing along to, laugh with, and cry to - it's quite a spectacle.
reviews.author: Paul Salfen

reviews.text: With some minor tweaks to breathe new life into the aquatic tale, The Little Mermaid is a vibrant and joyous adaptation.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: Are things better under the sea? Not in this live-action remake. There are some great performances though, from Bailey, Hauer-King and McCarthy, which kept things enjoyable.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: Despite the headlines, The Little Mermaid is a magical reimagining, one that may be too long or too scary for young children, but will surprise and delight older kids and grown fans of the original.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Vibrantly realized undersea with silky clarity, bursting with energy, color and cuteness. Poignant ending shows what it means to listen to someone's voice and let them find their own destiny. Comes to life with visual and voice, in more ways than one.
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: Halle Bailey does a great job taking on the challenging role of Ariel. Some of the visuals, particularly the underwater scenes with floating hair, left a bit to be desired and Melissa McCarthy could've been a bit more soulful as Ursula but it was fine.
reviews.author: Tatiana Albandos

reviews.text: It’s functionally good-natured rehash fare, bogged down by some watery CG and a few uncomfortable dips into “uncanny valley”, yet buoyed up by Bailey’s winning titular performance.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: A splashy mermaid performance by the vibrant, soulful and pleasant-voiced Halle Bailey.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: It’s well made to a point, and I think it will probably be great for many people, especially those who really loved the old film or want to see a Black Mermaid Princess.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: If you have any reason to watch this pallid remake of the 1989 film, watch it for Halle Bailey...
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: Halle Bailey. Enough said. Good night, everybody!
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Aside from Bailey's fantastic voice and a few song sequences, this movie feels like imagination in reverse. It limits creativity rather than expands it.
reviews.author: Doug Walker

reviews.text: Halle Bailey is a revelation. She is the heart and soul of this film, accompanied by wonderful performances by the cast all around. It is a wonderful addition to the story while still honoring the original. It is a treat!
reviews.author: Josie Meléndez

reviews.text: This is what happens when you start thinking of films as “content.”
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: A few minor missteps can't erase the fact that The Little Mermaid is one of Disney's best live-action remakes to date and a film that should entertain parents and children alike.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid is a total joy! Halle Bailey delivers a dazzling debut full of tenderness and genuine wonder with a voice that gives new dynamic life to these classic Disney songs. Rob Marshall directs a vibrant, captivating and truly touching film.
reviews.author: John Rocha

reviews.text: Imperfect, and too long, the film is saved by Halle Bailey, who shines through.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: McCarthy's dazzling replay of "Poor Unfortunate Souls" could be counted as the real musical showstopper, despite the top-notch array of other standard "Mermaid" tunes updated for the remake, including Oscar-winning Best Song "Under the Sea."
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Even though this live action remake has a few missteps, Halle Bailey is magical as Ariel . Alongside Melissa McCarthy as a deliciously delectable Ursula, together they make returning "under the sea" entertaining and fun for a whole new generation
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Halle Bailey is a superstar.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: It should be applauded for featuring merpeople from all backgrounds, for not airbrushing out Halle's acne scars and for carefully referencing ocean pollution.
reviews.author: Josh Saunders

reviews.text: This is a story about mermaids and magic and talking fish — it doesn’t need a political angle, or an unexpected family connection… or even an extra 52 minutes of screen time, in the end.
reviews.author: Liz Shannon Miller

reviews.text: The new Little Mermaid is no classic but it's a dependable half- term treat... or rather feast, given that it runs for almost an hour longer than the original.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: Disney transforms its 1989 animated version of Andersen’s story in such a way that its enchantment is deracinated. More care has gone into aquarium-style realism than into considering what the fantasy of otherness means.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Halle Bailey happens to be perfect: She has a clear, powerful voice -- able to unleash a tsunami of emotions when she sings the anthemic “Part of Your World” -- and her performance is appealingly playful and sweet, even relatable.
reviews.author: Tom Gliatto

reviews.text: Still, the positives outweigh the negatives and there are some nice touches that make this reimagining of the classic film worth your time.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: Halle Bailey will have to visit a chiropractor, because she alone carries this entire film on her shoulders. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Randy Meeks

reviews.text: While not earth-shattering, The Little Mermaid is a movie to take the whole family to, and my quibbles really are minor.
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: Just enough elements come together to justify why the retelling of this story works a tad bit better than other Disney attempts.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: Maybe in 30 years, when they do an animated remake of the live-action remake of the animated film, we’ll get a movie as brave as Ariel’s potential message and as entertaining as Bailey clearly is.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Despite all the flavors in the cast, the movie is still disappointingly vanilla.
reviews.author: Craig D. Lindsey

reviews.text: Suffers from the murky, underlit look common in Disney tentpoles. In underwater sequences the dimness ostensibly approximates realism, but the real function is to camouflage CGI quality issues. Too much fails at a basic level: It’s not worth looking at.
reviews.author: Steven D. Greydanus

reviews.text: There is comfort to be found here, and pure childlike delight. We can set the burdens of the world aside for a few hours and immerse ourselves in a world of creativity, color, music and imagination. There are far worse ways to escape.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: Director Rob Marshall is the key to uplifting the live action lushness, and Halle Bailey shuts down the debate, as her Ariel is luminous. The voices of Daveed Diggs and Awkwafina provides the animal comic relief. And we get to see a MerMan ... MerMan!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: The live-action version of The Little Mermaid ... is a thoroughly pleasant watch with some nice performances, which clears the bar for success for this era of Disney history.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid has plenty of neat, ostensibly progressive additions, but it is not the deep reimagining that Ariel’s story deserved.
reviews.author: Pravina Rudra

reviews.text: Was this live action remake really necessary? Probably not. But the new film retains all of the old magic with plenty of worthy add-ons. And Halle Bailey is a charmer who sings her heart out.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Disney recycles its seawater-soaked Cinderella, now in a live action musical.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: “The Little Mermaid” wasn’t meant for me. It was meant for the little girl in my row who excitedly yelped “Dad! Mermaids! Dad! Mermaids!” over and over during the first few minutes of the movie.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Bailey is very good. But this mess is almost one hour longer than the animated original. Mermaids' tales don't get better because they're longer.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: With Bailey’s remarkable talent and heavenly voice, the film can’t fail.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: What is different about this Little Mermaid is the mixture of races and the push to highlight the independence of today's Ariel, bringing the character to a more modern world. {Full Review in Spanish}
reviews.author: Laura Hiros

reviews.text: 'The Little Mermaid' is not just another useless, soulless remake from the Mouse House. Not only does it give the gift of Halle Bailey as Ariel, but it also fortifies its predecessor's story by adding much needed narrative context and emotional pull.
reviews.author: Francisca Tinoco

reviews.text: While it makes a harder case for its own identity more than most of the other remakes...it ultimately doesn’t rise to the level of truly essential. It’s true what they say: “Life’s full of hard choices, innit it?”
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: Halle Bailey proves to be the film’s strongest selling point, cutting an enchanting figure as she bashes out “Part of Your World” for all she’s worth.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: The beautiful animation that kicked off the Disney renaissance is recreated here with Windows 10 screensaver graphics.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: It’s just a serviceable attempt to do what the 1989 animated film did for Hans Christian Andersen’s original story from 1837—updating an old tale to appeal to contemporary tastes.
reviews.author: Collin Garbarino

reviews.text: The whole endeavor is also just a reminder that no movie should attempt underwater scenes in the wake of Avatar: The Way of Water. It all looks flat and washed out.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: While it can’t match the effortless charm of the 1989 animated classic, this overstuffed live-action echo fills the title role with shining new star Halle Bailey who gives this musical just the oomph it needs—a heart that sings and a spirit that soars.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: I'm looking forward to the animated remake in a few years. These Disney "live-action" movies are pointless, unless the entire point is to just make money. In which case, these are the most important films of all-time. The Little Mermaid is tedious.
reviews.author: Adam Olinger

reviews.text: The classic story gets a modern face-lift with fresh, diverse casting and some initially stunning effects that are marred by a murky action sequence that brings the film to a befuddling conclusion.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Yes, to have a Black princess in a major Hollywood film is, sadly, forward-thinking in 2023. But there is nothing innovative or reformist about what happens in this movie.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: Halle Bailey's performance keeps the film from drowning, but it still flounders quite a bit.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: The idea of re-doing Beauty and the Beast or The Lion King in slick but unconvincing live action seemed, beyond the obvious profit potential, gratuitous. Fine as the performers are, this Little Mermaid seems that way too.
reviews.author: M.V. Moorhead

reviews.text: For the most part, I had a good time at “The Little Mermaid.” The film is buoyed by its actors and some of its visuals.
reviews.author: Odie Henderson

reviews.text: While the original The Little Mermaid dazzled with its beautifully imaginative underwater kingdom and talking sea creatures, Rob Marshall's remake is a soulless cash grab utterly devoid of any hint of charm of visual whimsy
reviews.author: Kshitij Rawat

reviews.text: It adds hints of a complicated world beyond the narrow realms of fantasy; it delivers earnest cheer.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: For the poor, unfortunate souls hoping this The Little Mermaid will either equal or surpass the animated version, disappointment will be their unhappy bedfellow.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: There are some bright spots with the performances of Halle Bailey's Ariel and Melissa McCarthy's entertaining take on Ursula. Unfortunately, Rob Marshall's execution fails to bring this fairy tale to life.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: Marshall's movie ... does enough well that it's almost tempting to forgive the project of its more apparent flaws.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Adding 50 minutes of new material to the 1989 Disney classic, this live-action remake still feels like a pale imitation, exchanging stylish animation for uncanny CGI and poorly-shot musical numbers.
reviews.author: Gavia Baker-Whitelaw

reviews.text: Bailey is an amazing force to behold ... but everything else lacks her passion and innovation, foregoing any sort of compelling reason to watch.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: It’s better than most of these Disney cash grabs and worth seeing to witness the emergence of Bailey as a new star.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The worst and saddest thing about this new The Little Mermaid is to watch a purely mechanical and dead-eyed Sebastian conducting a colorful coral and marine fauna fête to the catchy and wonderful "Under The Sea." [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Stiletano

reviews.text: "The Little Mermaid" is an entertaining adaptation that deserves to make a big splash at the box office.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: All of this added material is superfluous and dramatically inert. Every extra minute feels like a betrayal of the original, in which not a word was wasted.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: [Rob Marshall] dives into The Little Mermaid without straying too far from the previous version, as someone who needs to swim close to the shore, but finds his stride by adding almost an hour of film to the original 83 minutes.
reviews.author: Nazareno Brega

reviews.text: The gorgeous animated film and spectacularly fun stage production have wowed audiences for over three decades, but now that Halle Bailey’s Ariel has become part of our world, it will be difficult to go back to them.
reviews.author: Maggie Lovitt

reviews.text: Part of that world of lazy remakes, alas. At least Sebastian the crab is still fun.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: It is a live-action remake that sometimes enjoys the voice and tenderness of Halle Bailey, but whose narrative core, I suspect, never escapes the boring and conventional formulas that get lost in the surface like fish in water. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Racist weirdos aside, this new The Little Mermaid is even less imaginative than you’d expect from one of the live-action remakes Disney now grinds out relentlessly.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: This is a beautiful and buoyant interpretation. And in Bailey, a major discovery brings oodles of heart and star-making talent to every frame.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: (Bailey's) rendition of Ariel’s signature song “Part of Your World” enthralls, and her sweet and spunky performance enchants. Bailey may be the standout, but she’s not the only noteworthy performer. Melissa McCarthy is wickedly campy...
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Frankly, this Ariel could do better.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: "The Little Mermaid" nicely balances the things it knows we expect from this story with dazzling new elements.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: While one can’t deny the effort that’s gone into this new, more expansive “Mermaid,”...it lumbers rather than soars...the littler “Little Mermaid” remains by far the better of the two.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Director Rob Marshall’s take on The Little Mermaid stays faithfully close to the ‘89 basics and many of the scene-by-scene, shot-by-shot design schemes of the animated version.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: This remake just sort of treads water, buoyed up by the excellence of the original.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: Diggs and Awkwafina – plus  Jacob Tremblay as the voice of a far-too-real Flounder – do what they can with some hit-and-miss dialogue as Ariel's sidekicks.
reviews.author: Shaye Weaver

reviews.text: Charming musical which will be relatable to the ‘Hamilton’ musical generation with impressive vocals, new songs and enthusiasm from Halle Bailey as Ariel ... Bailey is perfectly cast, with a wide-eyed innocence, and is indeed that star
reviews.author: Latoya Austin

reviews.text: The new film bursts with the same color and energy as its 1989 animated predecessor, it also manages to seamlessly interweave a relevant focus on women’s self-determination in a way that brings it into a modern age without losing its magical luster.
reviews.author: Chauncey K. Robinson

reviews.text: There’s little resisting Bailey’s portrayal of Ariel, which hits the right notes throughout.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: If you're a fan of the animated Little Mermaid, this remake isn't about to replace the original in your affection. But... For some kids, it may just be their new favourite thing, and a film that opens them up to a world of cinema, music, and fantasy.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: Actress and singer Halle Bailey took that huge expectation put on her shoulders and ran with it – she shines in the role of Ariel.
reviews.author: Audrey Donohue

reviews.text: Better than most of Disney's recent spate of remakes, but it's not as if the bar were set especially high. The human performances help offset the lack of emotion from the film's CGI creations, and the signature musical numbers still evoke strong emotions.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: A couple of ocean bound set pieces, plus a vibrant undersea world, gives the film plenty of visual spectacle, but when it aims for the audience’s heartstrings, the results are variable.
reviews.author: Freda Cooper

reviews.text: The charm of what did work seems so small, but it is the core of the film -- it's Ariel and Eric, and if you can stick that landing, you can have a sweet, enjoyable film for families that's just covered by a lot of annoyances.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: Halle Bailey cast as Ariel was outstanding. Her voice could move mountains, and all of the song choices were spectacular. The story was dry at moments with some horrific visuals for a few characters, but overall it's an enjoyable remake.
reviews.author: Brandon Avery

reviews.text: Most of the changes work and enrich the movie, while others are totally unnecessary and register as a discordant note that interrupts the musical ingenuity of the original material. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: In place of the film serving as a renaissance for Disney animation, this little remake champions exploration, diversity, and courage for all ages, providing a smarter successor that is (dare it be so?) better than the original.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid has a magical spell to weave, and it will surely be the favorite version of many out there who will cherish it as part of their world.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: With the exception of a few musical numbers, including a nicely choreographed “Under the Sea,” the film just oozes from scene to scene like a puddle of water creeping slowly across a floor.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: Whether or not this film will have much staying power, it’s doing what it can to be true to the original vision while only mildly getting in the way of itself. That’s enough to keep this film from being a poor unfortunate new version of a past Disney hit.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: It's no secret that the Disney version of The Little Mermaid doesn't have a whole lot in common with Hans Christian Andersen's original. It's a shame they didn't take as many liberties when they decided to remake their own version.
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: Disney’s most soulless, pointless live-action remake yet.
reviews.author: Suchin Mehrotra

reviews.text: Bailey’s Ariel is just so lovely and likable, we can’t help but root for her to win true love and prove that humankind and merpeople really aren’t so different after all.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: The film certainly looks and sounds pretty enough. The mandatory A+ production values and classic soundtrack sweep us up in a story that we probably know more thoroughly than The Three Little Pigs. (And, BTW, where is Disney's remake of that cartoon?)
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: ‘…the whole package shouldn’t offend the memory of those who enjoyed the original as kids…it’s a measure of how ground-breaking the 1989 film was that most of the elements still shine brightly today...'
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Halle Bailey brings the magic to The Little Mermaid, the enchantment of her voice compares to the most enticing of sirens, and in her gaze and smile she conveys Ariel’s curiosity and sense of adventure.
reviews.author: Ayelet Dekel

reviews.text: The remake of The Little Mermaid, as a whole, is serviceable at best with some very good moments. Melissa McCarthy is perfect as Ursula. It's probably one of her best performances yet.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: [Halle] Bailey’s casting and presence makes far more of an impact than the story does, but in spite of its superfluous nature, it’s charming and entertaining enough whilst it’s here.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Halle Bailey is a total powerhouse in this, and will make you weep with her rendition of “A Part Of Your World”. Melissa McCarthy is fantastic as Ursula. Some (new) songs were a bit forgettable…
reviews.author: Wendy Lee Szany

reviews.text: Telling the same story but with its own personality, and a wonderful Caribbean touch. Halle Bailey is charmingly charismatic... a fun, heartwarming experience, & the only adaptation that left me wanting to see it soon again. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: Without any nostalgic connection to the original property, The Little Mermaid is a peculiarly ambivalent experience, all its elevating touches counterbalanced by its new flaws.
reviews.author: Travis DeShong

reviews.text: Disney’s unsightly live action-remake of the 1989 classic drowns in the murky waters of ill-conceived VFX.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid is at its simplest the quintessential story of an outsider that everyone can connect with. In this modern retelling, many will walk away having fallen in love with Bailey’s Ariel, and feeling not only seen but also moved by her story.
reviews.author: Theolin Tembo

reviews.text: As valuable as this representation is, Hailey’s performance highlights that the spirit and character of Ariel transcend superficial differences -- qualities like independence, determination and ambition have no racial signature.
reviews.author: Niamh Jiménez

reviews.text: A fun if forgettable piece of entertainment.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: There are plenty of moments and scenes that work beautifully... but none of it adds up to much more than a piece of merchandise, produced by a corporation too big to risk originality.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: Bailey’s performance is a stunning, starmaking endeavor, proving herself a vividly talented name in the making (and her chemistry with Hauer-King helps sell the story).
reviews.author: Morgan Shaunette

reviews.text: Here’s an inescapable fact that’s been known by humans ever since they were bold enough to sail the seven seas: When you drag something from underwater to the surface, it ends up a limp, bedraggled mess.
reviews.author: Chris Rovzar

reviews.text: Bailey may have a good voice, but she doesn’t have the requisite on-screen charisma to break through Rob Marshall’s leaden direction and the uncanny valley sheen of all the CGI-augmented action.
reviews.author: Alastair McKay

reviews.text: Disney’s latest live action remake of one of their own animated classics, The Little Mermaid, is another bit of wading into the shallow end of the creativity pool.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: It's flat, dramatically vacant and visually inert, with a lead performance that all too closely resembles a fish out of water.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: While The Little Mermaid is far from being a complete disaster in the same way the remakes of Aladdin and Dumbo were, the film is a massive mixed bag.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: So maybe this "The Little Mermaid" has more to recommend it than I initially thought. If only it were cut down and sped up.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: It reeks of obligation and noble intentions. Joy, fun, mystery, risk, flavor, kink — they’re missing. The movie’s saying, “We tried!” Tried not to offend, appall, challenge, imagine.
reviews.author: Wesley Morris

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid benefits from its expanded run-time, and by committing to a showy tone that (mostly) works for a fun time.
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: Some poor, unfortunate souls will want more from Disney’s latest remake, but Halle Bailey shines even if the script stays pretty true to the animated original.
reviews.author: Sarah Marloff

reviews.text: The film's diverse casting has already made the point about unity, and done so much more eloquently. The Little Mermaid mostly avoids preaching, though. It remains what it always was: a charming, escapist fairy tale.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: We get to witness the rise of a star and The Little Mermaid becomes more swim than sink.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: An on-the-other-fin mixed bag of a movie that honors its source material with a big, color-saturated production, while never precisely proving that it ever needed to exist.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Halle Bailey’s charms can’t distract from all the bizarre choices at the heart of this underwhelming live-action remake.
reviews.author: Leila Latif

reviews.text: I was all in after seeing Halle Bailey’s stunning work as Ariel. She absolutely nails the part. Her rendition of “Part of Your World” is breathtaking with its build and the passion and drive Bailey puts into it.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Happily, [its] flaws aren’t enough to sink the film. Bailey’s Ariel is radiant throughout and, in places, Marshall’s hyper-stylized visuals add oomph and dazzle to the songs.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: Led by a star-making performance from the luminous Halle Bailey, the undeniably magical and terrifically delightful 'The Little Mermaid' hits that sweet spot between reinvention and nostalgia.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Although money was undoubtedly the primary driver for remaking The Little Mermaid, at least on this occasion the filmmakers have proven able to engage in something more than nostalgia-mining.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: When you hear Halle Bailey sing, there is no doubt. She crushes it and aces the biggest test this movie needed to pass.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: So much to love in director Rob Marshall’s live- action adaptation of THE LITTLE MERMAID. Not only does he have a splendid cast, but the entire film is amazing from beginning to end.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Guaranteed to enthrall a whole new generation of movie lovers as well as Baby Boomers on up. It has it all --- an engaging story, a tremendously likeable cast, glorious cinematography, a superb musical score, and a singular performance from Halle Bailey.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: There may not be any compelling reason for The Little Mermaid to exist, but it at least manages to be broadly entertaining while it is here.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: A joyous delight! Halle Bailey is tremendous, an absolute superstar! Despite some pacing issues, and middling new songs, it's amongst the best Disney remakes, and leaves you smiling from beginning to end. The movie is like a big warm hug.
reviews.author: Dave Lee

reviews.text: The live-action “Little Mermaid” is a fresh take on a beloved classic that isn’t afraid to take a fairy tale and make it as real as it can, inviting its audience to dive into uncharted waters alongside its engaging and charming central characters.
reviews.author: Lex Briscuso

reviews.text: If there was any reason for this remake in particular, it was to have Halle Bailey as Ariel!
reviews.author: Susan Kamyab

reviews.text: While none of Disney's live-action reboots are strictly necessary, there's a lot to enjoy about The Little Mermaid.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: Flipping its fins doesn’t get The Little Mermaid too far, but it’s one of the least surface-level Disney live-action remakes in a while.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: While The Little Mermaid is not the first live-action Disney movie ever put on the big screen, it’s definitely the best one yet.
reviews.author: Kayla Harrington

reviews.text: Halle Bailey was born to play Ariel! Her “Part Of Your World” is a true revelation. I love the new additions to the story that let her and Eric form a real connection. They were able to add suspense to a classic story we all know and love.
reviews.author: Kristen Maldonado

reviews.text: Ozempic Flounder aside, most of the alterations made to bring this tale of a curious young woman who longs to expand her universe, exchange her fins for feet, and stand tall are a positive step forward.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: Disney's live-action movies try to be more and more realistic while using and abusing digital effects, and they end up being more artificial than their animated counterparts. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: This film didn’t need to exist...
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: Rob Marshall keeps all the elements folks cherished about the cartoon intact while also introducing rising star Halle Bailey, who absolutely crushes the lead role of Ariel, to the world. And what a talent she is.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: The core story beats and songs are all intact, the visuals pop and the cast all embody the characters they are tasked with bringing to life. It isn't perfect and there some frustrating choices, but nevertheless should please fans old and new.
reviews.author: Kyle Wilson

reviews.text: Those who loved the original will find enough of it here to love it all over again, and those who never saw it will get a glimmer of it, but not quite the full shine and glow.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: Hold a grudge that classics should never be remade, I’m on that team, but you cannot argue the entertainment was delivered well enough here for its target audience.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Less heartfelt, funny, enchanting and exhilarating than the beloved animated classic. Why fix it if it ain't broken?
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: … may not always be better than the original, but as a newly plotted course through familiar waters, it avoids the turbulence that has capsized past remakes.
reviews.author: Cain Noble-Davies

reviews.text: An uneasy mix of carbon copy and superfluous added material, presented in “live-action” that looks and feels (and is) as artificial as Lightning McQueen. It’s diverting for an hour and a half, until you realize that there are 40 minutes of movie left.
reviews.author: Hillary Busis

reviews.text: The live action version gives more emotional depth to the story while some of the effects felt a bit shallow.  Awkwafina is alone a reason to watch the tale that remains timeless.
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: With her warm screen presence and incredible vocal range, Halle Bailey is easily the standout in what's otherwise yet another bland Disney live action remake. But at least it's one of the better ones. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mario Alegre

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid holds its own and finds glimpses of magic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mireia Mullor

reviews.text: The remake’s main sin... is that it’s visually confusing, if not altogether aesthetically unappealing.
reviews.author: Alex Abad-Santos

reviews.text: Although it falls short of the charm of the original film, The Little Mermaid is wonderful and shows how animated classics should be adapted in live action. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Jose Cruz

reviews.text: Thanks largely to star Halle Bailey, the lavish musical holds up nicely under the weight of those expectations, preserving the original’s essence while updating undernourished aspects of it and riding a warm, hard-to-resist wave of nostalgia.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: What works best are the elements it takes from the original... While this version doesn’t always find its sea legs, there’s enough of those original ideas recreated here that it can’t go too far wrong.
reviews.author: Alyssa Mora

reviews.text: For all its pizazz, everything about this Little Mermaid is just more muted. Miranda’s new songs are odd, too, and don’t seem to fit.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text:
I wouldn’t tell anyone NOT to see this movie. It is all about fan service and if you are a fan who wants this, you should try it… in a theater.

But it’s not a good movie.
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: Does a live-action The Little Mermaid feel vital? No. It gives fans of the animated original pretty much the same movie, beat for beat, with some slight adjustments that score on the positive side.
reviews.author: Tara Bennett

reviews.text: This film is not perfect and the climax is lacking. But it is charming, funny, and sincere and it makes me want to be part of that world.
reviews.author: Nicole Hill

reviews.text: “The Little Mermaid” origin story lacks room for this more feminist take. It simply is not deep enough.
reviews.author: Carla Meyer

reviews.text: “The Little Mermaid,” Disney's latest live-action remake, is surprisingly good. In fact, it is the best one yet.
reviews.author: Kaely Monahan

reviews.text: Maybe things are better under the sea, but they sure as hell aren’t better in live-action
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid captures the enchanting musical fantasy of the animated classic. Audiences will swoon as a beautiful mermaid falls in love with a dashing prince. Halle Bailey's soaring vocals and radiant energy illuminates the underwater depths.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: "The Little Mermaid" — a beloved 83-minute fairy tale transformed into a strained 135-minute pale imitation where the titular sea nymph doesn't get her Faustian legs until a full hour into the proceedings.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Perhaps I came in with low expectations, but the new The Little Mermaid turned out to be an acceptable update to the late '80s animated film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: The visual effects are uneven, and some of the characters are bland, but this live-action remake has enough appealing aspects to satisfy most viewers. Halle Bailey, Daveed Diggs, and Melissa McCarthy are the standout cast members.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: The music is still exceptional, but this modernization can’t come close to capturing the magic of its three-decades-older inspiration.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: The production of The Little Mermaid reveals the shortcomings of these adaptations. Not one single shot looks like they're actually underwater.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: One of the better reimagined Disney live action remakes because it stays true to the source material, features a terrific cast, and provides just enough magic, adventure, and romance to weather the storm.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Another ‘live-action’ remake that’s darker and less compelling than the animated original, but it’s saved by Bailey’s charming performance, McCarthy’s sass and the story’s own eternal magic.
reviews.author: Helen O'Hara

reviews.text: Halle Bailey’s Ariel is a delight – delivering the vocals to bring the original nostalgia to the surface. However, the 135 minute runtime doesn’t help matters, as somewhere along the way this remake lost the heart that made the original so special.”
reviews.author: Connor Petrey

reviews.text: Disney’s latest live-action “reimagining” of one of its animated musical classics, The Little Mermaid, succeeds largely because of three folks: leads Halle Bailey and Jonah Hauer-King and director Rob Marshall.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Halle is Ariel, totally and completely. Watch and you'll see, she'll be part of your world.
reviews.author: Tania Lamb

reviews.text: My nostalgia for the 1989 Little Mermaid, a movie I can quote by heart, has probably never been stronger than it is now. Neither has my wearied sense of déjà vu.
reviews.author: Aisha Harris

reviews.text: Occasionally, the familiar pleasure of this fish-out-of-water story cuts through the murky execution, like a trinket catching a ray of moonlight while sinking to the seafloor.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid is actually quite wonderful. It definitely captures the magic & essence of the original animated classic, while resulting in one of the better Disney live-action adaptations. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid (2023) is a beautifully animated live-action film that captures the heart of the first film, has original comedy that mostly works, & feels quick paced despite its longer duration. The new songs mostly fall flat, despite Scuttle's song.
reviews.author: Jason Escamilla

reviews.text: Though some renditions are a letdown from the animated classic, overall, The Little Mermaid is a sweet, magical adventure to enjoy with the family.
reviews.author: DarkSkyLady

reviews.text: A thoroughly entertaining, refreshingly impressive upgrade, respectful to the Disney original but with vibrant new jolts of movie magic, drama, danger, spectacle, joy, yearning, wit and romance.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: We’re given an occasionally charming, fairly rote rehash of the 1989 feature, now padded with extra songs, characters and conundrums that add very little to the magic of the original.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: Bailey gives a glowing performance of effortless starshine; her singing voice has both sweetness and power, and her smile is the sort on which dreams dance.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: In the end I loved Bailey so much as Ariel and her singing voice is so beautiful it allowed me to forgive much of the movies flaws. She really is that good.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: What’s on-screen too often feels like wan, second-rate imitation, and the few differences seem motivated less by a spirit of imagination than one of joyless anxiety.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Bailey sparkles in the role with a voice so ethereal it’s difficult to match and her performance is as gentle and as forceful as the seas themselves can be.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: It certainly helps to have Bailey in the lead role, with her performance pitch-perfect and her singing absolutely heavenly.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: A fun escape that is nostalgic for the 1989 original, but also manages to stand on its own as a film. Bailey & McCarthy are a little bland at first however both shine by the end of the movie. The cinematography is stunning. Perfect family entertainment.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid might be a story that audiences have already consumed hundreds of times — but thanks to the incredible performances and a whole lot of heart, this live-action iteration almost makes you feel like you're watching it for the first time.
reviews.author: Jenna Anderson

reviews.text: https://bleedingcool.com/movies/the-little-mermaid-review-lacks-the-courage-to-do-its-own-thing/
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: Decent enough but did a live action Little Mermaid film really need to be made?
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: It's not the worst Disney live action remake I've seen. But most of the original Disney magic is lost at sea.
reviews.author: Christie Cronan

reviews.text: A mixed bag overall, but still a must-see for Halle Bailey's breathtaking work as Ariel and Melissa McCarthy's deliciously devilish Ursula.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: Marshall, known for big, theatrical numbers, brings that same enthusiasm to this project.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: This Little Mermaid feels more or less like two-hour-plus cosplay with the texture and gravitas of a Disneyland sideshow.
reviews.author: Greg Nussen

reviews.text: Fantastic performances and a few smart updates aside, Marshall largely delivers the same paint-by-numbers story in a longer movie that should've pushed the bar more with its antagonist instead of wasting time on forgettable new songs.
reviews.author: Kirsten Acuna

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid, despite a few misfires, is one of Disney’s best live-action reimaginings to date.
reviews.author: Emily Zemler

reviews.text: Halle Bailey is tremendous as Ariel, providing powerful, emotion-stirring vocals & a wonderful sense of curiosity. New musical numbers, a slightly updated setting, and Daveed Diggs as Sebastian are other highlights in one of Disney's best remakes yet.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: Despite real actors, CGI and brand new material, “Mermaid” is the studio’s latest flesh-and-blood cash grab that’s more lifeless than far better two-dimensional painted drawings.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid is arguably the best live-action Disney remake since Kenneth Branagh’s Cinderella. The splendor is there; the romance is crafted with care — but something’s still missing.
reviews.author: Lyvie Scott

reviews.text: The unlikeliest modern love story of the year.
reviews.author: Joey Morona

reviews.text: Bailey has a beautiful singing voice, one which transports familiar Menken songs...into new heights…one of McCarthy’s all time best performances, the actress commanding her scenes, singing in a husky voice and vamping like a Broadway diva.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: As Ariel, Halle Bailey shines brighter than the sun. She’ll silence the haters easily.
reviews.author: Sarah Musnicky

reviews.text: So much goes wrong that it clouds any of the few bright spots. With that extra hour of runtime, you'd think they'd least bring the spectacle.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: While it’s still an exercise in re-branding and revenue, the results at least provide some dazzle, some romance, and a handful of pretty-good new songs with lyrics by Lin-Manuel Miranda.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: [S]ub-par CGI effects and clunky changes to Howard Ashman’s classic songs often make it feel like [Halle] Bailey is left to carry the movie on the strength of her remarkable talent alone.
reviews.author: Shannon Campe

reviews.text: Altogether charming, thoughtful and romantic.
reviews.author: Peter Martin

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid might not match the greatness of the original, but it’s the rare remake that feels worthy of being part of our world.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: But, in the end, the notes of real emotion are offered by Bardem with some sweet line readings and a tear-stained close-up that suggests there is indeed a tiny sliver of heart in this all-singing, all-splashing spectacle.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Halle Bailey’s rich performance makes the film worth watching; she was born to play Ariel.
reviews.author: Sophia Ciminello

reviews.text: Halle Bailey's version of “Part of Your World” has bore itself into my psyche — and likely the rest of the audience if judging by the applause break after her final ethereal riff.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Its most iconic moments are borrowed and copied wholesale, serving as little more than a reminder of simpler days watching clamshell VHS tapes released from the Disney Vault. Maybe that’s enough for some people. But maybe, like Ariel, we should want more.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: It isn’t all prefect, but The Little Mermaid is the best of Disney’s live action adaptations yet — and it’s not even close. Halle Bailey has proven herself as a true Disney Princess.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: While it has choppy waters at times, leading lady Halle Bailey, who is on her way to stardom, helps keep this classic together.
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: The live-action version of The Little Mermaid has awesome music as expected but the film itself is way too long at 135 minutes.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: At a hefty 2 hours and 15 minutes, 'The Little Mermaid' delivers more than enough content to fill it wisely, using just enough nostalgia to hook the adults and adding just enough new to entertain the kids.
reviews.author: Stacey Yvonne

reviews.text: It’s masterfully directed and features strong vocals that are guaranteed to distract you from the big, scary moments.
reviews.author: Raven Brunner

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid delivers for fans new and old, and Halle Bailey is a bonafide superstar.
reviews.author: Corey Chichizola

reviews.text: A thoroughly pointless cash grab of a thing, this new Little Mermaid is one of the most uninspired films to slither out of Disney since the company started raiding its own vault...
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: It seems we’ve finally been presented with a remake that has something to say. And most of this is down to a star-making turn from leading lady Halle Bailey.
reviews.author: Tori Brazier

reviews.text: As the studio has done with other live-action remakes, Disney betrays its own lack of imagination and an essential misreading of what made its original children’s fare such a joy to audiences in the first place.
reviews.author: Angelica Jade Bastién

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid may have a modernised take on the 1989 feature with a charming lead performance from Halle Bailey, but there is not enough to lift this live-action adaptation, resulting in a soulless and pointless remake.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: As The Little Mermaid crawls by at a snail's pace, the wondrous moments are weighed down by wasted opportunities for spectacle, emotion, and unapologetic bombast.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Lin-Manuel Miranda’s presence adds a welcome rap and steel-pan funk to the otherwise decorous soundtrack.
reviews.author: Alex Diggins

reviews.text: The film is far from a mere remake; it expands the universe of the original movie, with a sprawl that jumps off the screen and directly into its viewers’ hearts.
reviews.author: Coleman Spilde

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid is popping candy for the soul.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: While not everything goes swimmingly, Halle Bailey splendidly buoys this "Mermaid" as the naive underwater youngster with dreams of exploring the surface.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: What makes The Little Mermaid isn’t whether the fish look good, or what exactly fuels Triton and Ursula’s feud. It all comes back to Ariel and her journey, which is fueled by the central romance between her and Eric.
reviews.author: Petrana Radulovic

reviews.text: The Little Mermaid is the best live-action film adaptation of a Disney animation.
reviews.author: Swara Salih

reviews.text: Led by a pitch-perfect Halle Bailey, The Little Mermaid is bolstered by deeper characterization and a grand scope, even as it grapples with flaws.
reviews.author: Rachel LaBonte

reviews.text: Disney fans and casual moviegoers will enjoy the magic that The Little Mermaid brings to the big screen.
reviews.author: Joshua Mackey

reviews.text: Halle Bailey is all the reason that any audience should need to justify Disney revisiting this classic.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Marshall has made a movie with all the magic required to pull it off and, if not replace the original in our hearts, at least has made a movie that can stand next to that one to also become a memorable part of our cinematic world.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: With Halle Bailey, life under the sea is better than anything Disney live-action has done in nearly a decade.
reviews.author: Maureen Lee Lenker

reviews.text: A ho-hum adaptation buoyed by a lovely lead turn.
reviews.author: Lovia Gyarkye

reviews.text: "The Little Mermaid" is a live-action remake done well.
reviews.author: Vanessa Armstrong

reviews.text: For now, “The Little Mermaid” exists outside of the very world it so wants to be a part of, one already so lovingly rendered in its predecessor, “real” or not.
reviews.author: Kate Erbland

reviews.text: ...new additions fall flat, with the film ultimately proving to be another one of these remake projects that do little to improve upon the original or offer much in the way of a convincing reason to be beyond being a surefire cash-in.
reviews.author: Andrew Gaudion

reviews.text: A sparkling, enchanting new spin that out-swims the original, with a pitch-perfect performance from Halle Bailey.
reviews.author: Molly Edwards

reviews.text: There’s a real stink of obligation to everything that exists around Bailey and her star-making turn.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Bailey is both the finished film’s only unmitigated triumph and the best argument for this whole live action remake enterprise in one shimmering mermaidcore package.
reviews.author: Ellen E Jones

reviews.text: The slow pacing, often-overwrought emotion and undeniably outdated story mean that it fails to make much of a splash.
reviews.author: Nikki Baughan

reviews.text: Bailey grounds the film with her remarkable and sincere performance.
reviews.author: Britany Murphy

reviews.text: Although The Little Mermaid, Disney’s latest live-action remake, isn’t a mess as a whole, it leaves much to be desired.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: The otherwise controversial live-action remake gets a mostly better-than-expected boost from a stellar cast.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: It's hard not to be swept up in the sumptuous sentimentality all over again and give yourself over to that classic Disney magic.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

synopsis: The youngest of King Triton's daughters, and the most defiant, Ariel longs to find out more about the world beyond the sea, and while visiting the surface, falls for the dashing Prince Eric. While mermaids are forbidden to interact with humans, Ariel must follow her heart. She makes a deal with the evil sea witch, Ursula, which gives her a chance to experience life on land, but ultimately places her life -- and her father's crown -- in jeopardy.
